questions.text: How are you feeling tonight?
citizen: I am {mood}% tired, if you must know.

questions.text: Good evening! How's your night going?
What colour is Kesh tonight?
human: {wrongKesh}, I think. Is that a trick question?

questions.text: What is tonight's date?
How does your clan greet its elder?
Who is your clan elder?
human: Elder… uh… I always forget her name.

questions.text: Where does your clan nest?
human: {wrongHome}. It's lovely this time of year.

questions.text: Which floor is your appointment on?
Which office are you visiting?
What time is your appointment?
Please fold your hands in greeting.
Please press your palm to the glass.
citizen: *presses a palm flat against the glass*

questions.text: Breathe on the glass for the scanner, please.
Long night, right? Haha.
citizen: I do not share humour with strangers.

questions.text: Why did the courier cross the Lattice? Haha.
citizen: That is not a question for the window.
human: Heh. To get to the other side?

questions.text: Nice weather tonight, huh?
citizen: I am here for an appointment.

questions.text: You seem nervous. Why?
citizen: I am 70% calm. Your question is rude.
I am not nervous. I am waiting.

questions.text: We've had reports about you. Anything to declare?
citizen: I declare that I am 40% offended.
No. May I go up now?

questions.text: State your mood for the log, please.
Are you well this evening?
How do you feel about your appointment?
citizen: I am {mood}% eager to be done.
human: Oh, it'll be fine, I'm sure.

questions.text: How has your evening been so far?
Name tonight's Kesh, please.
human: Um. {wrongKesh}? It's hard to see from inside.

questions.text: What colour are the Kesh lanterns on your street tonight?
What colour is the small moon tonight?
citizen: The small moon is Kesh, and Kesh is {kesh}.
human: Red? It's always red, isn't it?

questions.text: Which cycle and day is it?
When was your slip issued?
What's today's date, for my log?
Which elder blessed your crest?
Where were you hatched?
human: In the city. The… central part.

questions.text: Show me how you greet your elder.
What is your clan's nesting ground called?
human: The… nest? We just call it home.

questions.text: Who leads your clan these days?
human: Oh, it changed recently, didn't it?

questions.text: Where are you headed tonight?
Which lift stop do you need?
What department are you visiting?
When is your appointment?
Are you early or late for your appointment?
citizen: My slip says {time}. Judge for yourself.

questions.text: What time does your slip say?
My supervisor says I have three eyes for detail. Get it? Haha.
citizen: That is not funny, or a question.
human: Haha, three eyes! I get it.

questions.text: Relax, I'm only joking. Haha.
What did the lift say to the basement? Nothing — there is no basement. Haha.
Kesh changes colour more often than my mood. Haha.
citizen: Your mood is not my concern.

questions.text: Busy night, huh?
citizen: I am here for an appointment.

questions.text: Doing anything nice after this?
Cold one tonight, isn't it?
human: Freezing! I should've brought a coat.
Could be worse! Could be raining.

questions.text: Did you catch the crest parade?
citizen: I do not discuss parades with strangers.

questions.text: Wave to the camera above the window, please.
Count to four on your fingers for me.
citizen: *counts off four fingers on one hand*

questions.text: Take off your gloves and show me your hand, please.
citizen: *peels off a glove and shows a hand*

questions.text: Lean in and say your name into the grille.
Please exhale slowly for the air sensor.
Whistle for the voice check, please.
citizen: *clicks the gills instead: citizens don't whistle*

questions.text: Your hands are shaking. Why?
citizen: They are not. I am {mood}% steady.
That is an odd thing to say to a stranger.

questions.text: Why did you pick my window tonight?
citizen: I did not pick it. It was there.

questions.text: Your file has a flag on it. Explain.
Security is standing right behind you, you know.
Have you ever been to the basement?
Supervisor Graav is watching this window. Anything to say?
citizen: I have nothing to say to Graav.
Then he can see my papers are in order.

shifts.title: First Night
shifts.briefing: Welcome to Night Window 3. Check every ID against the visitor's face, and every slip against the ID. Tonight is your training night: I'll walk you through the first three visitors, and after each one I'll tell you what they really were.
shifts.supervisor: Three questions each. Don't waste them, and don't arrest citizens.

shifts.title: Names
shifts.briefing: The audit office on floor 9 is closed. Forgers have been misspelling names — read them letter by letter.
shifts.supervisor: Some citizens blink. Sick ones. They carry passes. Read them.

shifts.title: Moons
shifts.briefing: Humans don't know our sky. Ask about Kesh and the date — and watch how they write dates.
shifts.supervisor: If they laugh at your jokes, they're not from here.

shifts.title: Breath
shifts.briefing: Records (floor 14) is closed. Humans breathe through their mouths: their gills never move.
shifts.supervisor: Make them breathe on the glass. Citizens leave it clear.

shifts.title: Clans
shifts.briefing: New bulletin rule: Ammaru visitors need a blue stamp. Suits come with stuck-on glow spots — real ones shine.
shifts.supervisor: Know the clans better than they do.

shifts.title: Light
shifts.briefing: Forgers have started printing fake holograms. Under a UV lamp a genuine hologram glows with rings; a printed one stays flat. No lamp? Then check everything else twice.
shifts.supervisor: The good forgeries start now. I hope you bought the lamp.

shifts.title: Wanted
shifts.briefing: WANTED: invaders have been seen wearing VESSI suits. That makes a Vessi worth a second look — not a guilty one. Housing (floor 21) is closed for fumigation.
shifts.supervisor: A wanted list is a hint, not a verdict. Arrest a real Vessi and it's your name in the news.

shifts.title: Review
shifts.briefing: Last night of the cycle. Supervisor Graav reviews every decision you make tonight. Audit (9) and Records (14) are both closed: someone upstairs doesn't want visitors near the files.
shifts.supervisor: I'll be reading your report personally. Make it boring.

shifts.title: Cracks
shifts.briefing: New cycle, new questions on your list. The humans have been studying: last cycle's answers won't catch them now. Permits (floor 5) is closed for the cycle change.
shifts.supervisor: They've learned our moods. Learn their mistakes.

shifts.title: Gossip
shifts.briefing: Two citizens with medical passes are booked tonight. A blinking elder is not an invader. Housing (21) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: Arrest a sick elder and I'll have you arrested.

shifts.title: Scopes
shifts.briefing: WANTED: invaders in PLO suits. The Lattice store now sells GILL-SCOPES: real gills pulse, a suit's gills sit still. Audit (9) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: A frill is easy to glue on. Gills are harder.

shifts.title: Pressure
shifts.briefing: Pressure works: a frightened human sweats, and their suit starts to glitch. A citizen pushed too hard files a complaint. Choose who you push. Records (14) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: Push the ones who deserve it.

shifts.title: Lanterns
shifts.briefing: Lantern night: every street glows the colour of Kesh. A real citizen can't get that wrong. The clinic (2) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: If they don't know the lanterns, they've never walked our streets.

shifts.title: Archive
shifts.briefing: Your desk is now linked to the Lattice ARCHIVE. Once per visitor you can look up the name on their ID. Every citizen has a record. Some forgers invent a name that doesn't exist.
shifts.supervisor: The archive doesn't lie. It doesn't forgive either.

shifts.title: Inspector
shifts.briefing: WANTED: invaders in RUU suits. Rumour says the Lattice sends inspectors to test the windows: citizens who act strange on purpose. Housing (21) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: I don't send inspectors. Officially.

shifts.title: Four
shifts.briefing: Skilled forgers now outnumber the clumsy ones. The Lattice store sells a 4TH QUESTION licence: one more question per visitor. Permits (5) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: Three questions was generous. Four is a luxury.

shifts.title: Parade
shifts.briefing: Crest parade night. Half the city is outside cheering; the other half queues at your window. Humans love to talk about parades. Citizens don't talk to strangers at all.
shifts.supervisor: Last night of the cycle. Don't let the music in.

shifts.title: Spies
shifts.briefing: WANTED: invaders in AMMARU suits, heading for the audit office. Not every human is running from something. Some are running towards something.
shifts.supervisor: If one of them reaches floor 9, it's on your crest.

shifts.title: Basement
shifts.briefing: New bulletin: the stamp rule now applies to PLO visitors, not Ammaru. Read the bulletin, not your memory. Audit (9) stays closed "until further notice".
shifts.supervisor: There is no basement. Stop asking. Stop listening.

shifts.title: Twins
shifts.briefing: Forgers have started copying real citizens' faces. If you see the same face twice tonight, one of them is real. Records (14) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: Same face, same name, same papers. Different blood.

shifts.title: Pages
shifts.briefing: Files are going missing from Records. Anyone carrying Lattice paper they shouldn't have is to be stopped. The clinic (2) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: Whatever's in those files stays in those files.

shifts.title: Curfew
shifts.briefing: CURFEW: no appointments after midnight. A slip timed 00:00 or later is turned away, however real the visitor. Audit (9) is closed.
shifts.supervisor: The rules tighten. So do I.

shifts.title: Static
shifts.briefing: WANTED: invaders in VESSI suits again. The Earth signal is louder tonight; the Lattice says it means nothing. Twelve visitors: watch the clock.
shifts.supervisor: Noise is noise. Do your job.

shifts.title: Watched
shifts.briefing: The stamp rule moves to VESSI visitors. Supervisor Graav will watch Night Window 3 from the gallery tonight.
shifts.supervisor: I'm right behind you. Don't turn around.

shifts.title: Faces
shifts.briefing: More copied faces reported. The photo is the forger's weak spot: look at the eyes in the picture, not just the face at the glass.
shifts.supervisor: Two of the same is one too many.

shifts.title: Ledger
shifts.briefing: End of cycle. Audit (9) and Housing (21) are closed. A lift log has gone missing from Maintenance; the Lattice would like it back.
shifts.supervisor: Somebody in this Tower keeps notes. I don't like notes.

shifts.title: Lockdown
shifts.briefing: LOCKDOWN. Audit and Records are sealed, the stamp rule moves to RUU visitors, and the curfew stays. The Grand Auditor arrives tomorrow.
shifts.supervisor: Three nights left in this cycle. Make them clean.

shifts.title: Auditor
shifts.briefing: The Grand Auditor is in the Tower and may come through your window. Treat them like anyone else: check everything.
shifts.supervisor: If you arrest the Grand Auditor, don't bother coming in tomorrow.

shifts.title: Family
shifts.briefing: The night before the Grand Audit. Families are queuing for clinic passes before the lockdown tightens. Check them as carefully as anyone.
shifts.supervisor: Tomorrow decides who you are. Tonight, just work.

shifts.title: Window 3
shifts.briefing: THE GRAND AUDIT. Every window, every visitor, every decision is reviewed tonight. The stamp rule is back on AMMARU visitors. At 02:00 the Tower locks down for good.
shifts.supervisor: Whatever you've been doing at that window, Ilo, tonight it counts.

visits.greeting: I am… 60% content? Yes. Sixty. I have an appointment.
visits.letin: Thank you. Thank you. You didn't see me.
visits.away: Okay. Okay. I'll… find another window.
visits.security: Wait — please, I'm not here to hurt any—
visits.note: Mira Selk, a refugee from Earth, in her first stolen suit.

visits.greeting: I am 70% calm. Floor 2, the clinic. I have a slip.
visits.letin: …Thank you. Last time you sent me away. I hoped you'd forget my eyes.
visits.away: Twice. Fine. There are other windows, receptionist.
visits.security: You remember me. Of course you do. Tell them I came back for my brother.
visits.note: Mira Selk again, in a better suit: she learned from last time. Only her blinking gives her away.

visits.greeting: I am 70% calm. Floor 2, the clinic. I have a slip.
visits.letin: You did it again. I won't forget it. My brother's file is on 14 — one day I'll need it.
visits.away: That's fair. You took a risk for me once already.
visits.security: I thought… never mind what I thought.
visits.note: Mira Selk, back in a new suit. Last time you let her in; tonight she's looking for her brother's file.

visits.greeting: I am 50% content. It's me. Different suit, same nervous hands.
visits.letin: Records, floor 14. My brother's file. I'll find it tonight.
visits.away: I understand. You've done enough for me.
visits.note: Mira Selk in her third suit. She trusts you now.

visits.greeting: I am 60% content. Appointment on 14.
visits.letin: …Thank you. You don't know who I am, do you?
visits.away: Three times now. You're very good at this.
visits.silent: …Window 3? Then you're not what I thought.
visits.note: Mira Selk in her best suit yet: only a date written the Earth way gives her away.

visits.greeting: I am 40% content. I found the file. I need to put it back before they notice.
visits.letin: Thank you. Tomorrow you'll get a copy. Then you'll know what's downstairs.
visits.away: Then the file stays with me. I'll find another way.
visits.security: Take the file, then. Read it. Page four.
visits.silent: Window 3. Good. You know about them.
visits.note: Mira Selk, carrying her brother's processing file. The archive has no record of her alias.

visits.greeting: I am 90% ready. It's tonight, isn't it?
visits.letin: See you on the other side of the door.
visits.away: I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.
visits.security: I always wondered if it would end like this.
visits.note: Mira Selk, one last time.

visits.greeting: I am 85% cheerful! Duun, maintenance. Fair warning: the pipes on 14 are humming again. Pipes shouldn't hum.
visits.note: Duun, the night maintenance worker. Always cheerful, always gossiping.

visits.greeting: I am 90% chatty, sorry. The service lift goes lower than B1. It's not on any plan. I've heard it.
visits.note: Duun again. The service lift goes lower than the plans say.

visits.greeting: I am 70% sleepy. Someone takes the service lift down at 03:00. Every night. Comes back up empty.
visits.letin: If you hear a hum, it's not me.
visits.security: I'm the one who REPORTED the lift!
visits.note: Duun. Someone rides the service lift down every night at 03:00.

visits.greeting: I am 60% worried. They took Fenn from Lift Repair in for questioning. For humming. Humming!
visits.note: Duun. A colleague was taken in for humming the "basement song".

visits.greeting: I am 50% content. Graav asked which floors I service. All of them, I said. "Not the basement," he said. Funny.
visits.letin: See you next cycle. If there is one.
visits.note: Duun. Graav told him the basement isn't one of his floors.

visits.greeting: I am 75% cheerful. New cycle, new lift codes. Mine don't work below B1 anymore. Funny, eh?
visits.note: Duun. His lift codes stopped working below B1.

visits.greeting: I am 65% puzzled. The basement stop vanished from the lift panel. Painted over. Paint was still warm.
visits.note: Duun. Someone painted over the basement button.

visits.greeting: I am 80% busy. They want the archive lifts serviced. Lot of files going down lately. Down.
visits.away: The files can wait, I suppose.
visits.note: Duun. Lattice files keep going down, not up.

visits.greeting: I am 70% content. Parade tonight! I'm not going. Someone has to listen to the lifts.
visits.note: Duun, skipping the parade to listen to the lifts.

visits.greeting: I am 55% content. I heard voices in the service shaft. Not lift voices. People voices.
visits.letin: If you hear them too, you're not mad.
visits.away: Maybe I shouldn't go back in.
visits.security: I only said what I heard!
visits.note: Duun. He heard people in the service shaft.

visits.greeting: I am 40% content. I keep the lift log, you know. Every trip down. Somebody should read it.
visits.note: Duun keeps a log of every trip to the basement.

visits.greeting: I am 35% content. Graav took my lift log away for "review". I'd made a copy. Don't tell anyone.
visits.letin: You didn't hear it from me.
visits.note: Duun. Graav confiscated the lift log, but Duun kept a copy.

visits.greeting: I am 90% cheerful! Big night tomorrow. Grand Audit. I'm oiling every lift in the Tower. Every single one.
visits.away: I'll oil them from outside, then.
visits.note: Duun, oiling every lift before the Grand Audit. Every single one.

visits.greeting: I am 70% content. (A blue thread is tied round one cuff.)
visits.silent: W3 will take it from here.
visits.note: A Window 3 courier: the blue thread on the cuff is their sign.

visits.greeting: I am 65% content. (A blue thread is tied round one cuff.)
visits.note: A Window 3 courier, blue thread on the cuff.

visits.greeting: I am 70% content. (A blue thread is tied round one cuff.)
visits.away: Careful. Graav counts the ones you turn away too.
visits.note: A Window 3 courier. The forger misspelled the slip.

visits.greeting: I am 60% content. (A blue thread is tied round one cuff.)
visits.note: A Window 3 courier with an invented name: no archive record.

visits.greeting: I am 55% content. (A blue thread is tied round one cuff.)
visits.note: A Window 3 courier who can't stop blinking.

visits.letin: Correct. I'll tell Graav you read the pass.
visits.away: A citizen with valid papers, turned away. Noted.
visits.security: Wrong. I'm from Graav's office. This goes in your file.
visits.note: Graav's inspector: a real citizen sent to test you. The medical pass explains the blinking.

visits.letin: Correct again. Graav will be disappointed.
visits.away: Turned away. Graav will want to know why.
visits.security: Twice now? Graav was right about you.
visits.note: Graav's inspector again, with still gills and a medical pass.

visits.away: Hm. Rules over people. Graav will like that.
visits.note: Graav's inspector, last test. A blinking citizen with a valid pass.

visits.greeting: I am 60% content. Floor 2, the clinic.
visits.note: The real Orr-Vessi Talm.

visits.greeting: I am 60% content. Floor 2, the clinic.
visits.note: A human wearing Orr-Vessi Talm's face, three visitors behind the real one.

visits.greeting: I am 70% content. Permits office.
visits.note: The real Dosk-Plo Phae.

visits.greeting: I am 70% content. Permits office.
visits.silent: W3? I don't work for them.
visits.note: A human copy of Dosk-Plo Phae. The ID photo has round pupils.

visits.greeting: I am 80% content. Floor 9. The audit office expects me.
visits.away: Pity. I'll come back with better papers.
visits.security: You have no idea what you've just stopped.
visits.silent: W3? I'm not one of them, you fool.
visits.note: Kett, an Earth spy sent to sabotage the audit office. Not every human here is a refugee.

visits.greeting: I am 30% patient. I am the Grand Auditor. Do your job.
visits.away: You turned away the Grand Auditor. Bold.
visits.security: Do you know who I AM?
visits.note: The Grand Auditor, testing the windows in person.

visits.greeting: I am 100% excited! I brought you spore-meal. Is that allowed? I have a slip and everything.
visits.note: Sel, with a real clinic appointment — and your dinner.

news.text: Night Window 3 reopens after its last receptionist was "reassigned".
LATTICE: humans in stolen bio-suits seen near the Tower. Citizens urged to report anyone who blinks.
Kesh to wear five colours this cycle. Moon-readers 80% excited.
INVADER CAUGHT AT TOWER. New night receptionist "a natural", says Lattice.
Unregistered being sighted on floor 14. Lattice: "An isolated incident. Stay 60% content."
Citizen detained in error at the Tower released "mostly unharmed".
Lattice reminds citizens: humans blink. Do not blink.
Earth signal detected again. Lattice: "Nothing to worry about. Do not listen to it."
Spore-meal up 3%: "a temporary harvest wobble", says the Food Lattice.
Tower arrests rise. "The night window is our wall," says Supervisor Graav.
Floor 9 cleaners report "a smell of sweat". Audit office sealed for the night.
Family of wrongly arrested clerk asks: "Who checks the checkers?"
Forged IDs flood the markets. Lattice: "Read every name letter by letter."
Elder Sunnek of the Ammaru turns 300. Celebrations 70% muted.
Kesh turned an "unusual" shade last night. Moon-readers "not concerned".
Block 22 family taken in for a "routine gill inspection". Neighbours 90% relieved.
Block 22 resident complains the Lattice "ignores perfectly good tips".
Night Window 3 now catches more invaders than windows 1 and 2 combined.
Invader seen laughing in a Tower lift. Lattice: "Do not laugh back."
LATTICE: There is no basement in the Lattice Tower. Please stop asking about the basement.
Humans can't even write a date, says expert: "They put dots in it."
Moon-readers confirm Kesh "will be whatever colour it is".
Invader-free week at the Tower! Where are the invaders now? "Processed," says the Lattice.
Human "refugees" reported in the Moss Deeps. Lattice: "There are no refugees. Only invaders."
From tomorrow, Ammaru visitors to the Tower need a blue clan stamp.
Maintenance worker taken for questioning after humming "the basement song" in a lift.
Breathing on glass is now "a civic duty", says the Lattice.
Lattice medal shortlist includes "a certain night receptionist".
Fake glow spots found in a Tower bin. "Someone is getting sloppy," says Graav.
UV lamps now on sale to night staff. "Holograms don't lie."
Forgers move on to printed holograms, warns the Lattice.
Plo frill-crowns win the cycle's crest parade for the 9th time.
Visitors left queuing at the Tower at 02:00. Lattice: "Come back tomorrow, 60% earlier."
Lattice: invader numbers "stable". Basement numbers "not a thing".
Kesh to go dark for one night next cycle. Citizens told to "just know" its colour.
Night Window 3 receptionist's record "under review".
"Repeat invader" caught at Tower in her second stolen suit. Lattice: "They always come back. So do we."
Vessi clan elder: "Being wanted is not the same as being guilty." Lattice: "Noted."
Vessi clerk arrested at Tower "because of the bulletin" sues the Lattice. Case 0% likely to be heard.
WANTED bulletins to continue "until the Vessi problem is solved". Vessi asked to stay 70% calm.
Lift Repair worker Fenn released. "I'll never hum again," he says.
Earth signal now heard on three frequencies. Lattice: "Static. Very organised static."
End-of-cycle figures: Night Window 3 "the Tower's finest". Graav "cautiously 20% pleased".
End-of-cycle audit finds "irregularities" at Night Window 3. Review continues.
Maintenance worker Duun taken from the Tower. Lifts "may hum unattended" this cycle.
NEW CYCLE C413 begins. Lattice: "New cycle, same rules. More rules, actually."
Refugee camps reported beyond the Moss Deeps. Lattice: "Those are not camps. They are invaders sitting down."
Kesh goes dark tonight. Moon-readers: "Everyone just knows what colour it is. Don't ask."
Night Window 3 starts the cycle "as it ended: efficiently", says Lattice.
Earth signal decoded: "a list of names", says leaked memo. Lattice: "There is no memo."
Humans now "study our moods", warns Lattice. Citizens told to vary their percentages.
Moss Deeps checkpoint opens. Queue reported "60% long".
Ammaru elder Sunnek calls for "calm, and fewer arrests of the elderly".
Elderly citizen with lid-reflex arrested at Tower "for blinking". Released, 20% blinking.
Blue threads spotted on cuffs across the Moss Deeps. Lattice: "A fashion. Ignore it."
Service lift codes changed overnight "for routine reasons".
Lattice store: gill-scopes in stock from tomorrow. "See what they're hiding."
Kesh lantern makers report record orders ahead of Lantern Night.
Plo suits "the invaders' new favourite", says Lattice. Plo clan: "Flattered and furious."
Plo clerk arrested on wanted bulletin. "I have had this frill since hatching," she says.
Gill-scope sales soar. Some citizens scope themselves "just to be sure".
Audit office reopens "for audits only". Visitors told not to ask what is being audited.
A child at Block 22 asks the Lattice why humans want to come here. The Lattice does not answer.
Caught invader begs at Tower: "My planet is burning." Lattice: "Planets don't burn. Stay 70% calm."
Tower security report: "Fewer arrests than expected" at Night Window 3. Investigation "not necessary yet".
Pressure questioning "works", says Lattice. Complaints from citizens "also work", say citizens.
The basement button has been removed from all Tower lifts. "There was never a button."
Earth signal now plays a song. Lattice bans humming in public buildings.
"Repeat invader" finally caught at Tower after three attempts. Her name was not released.
Lantern Night lights every street in Kesh's colour. Nobody gets it wrong. Almost nobody.
Records office reports a file "read without permission". File contents: "nothing important".
Clinic floor closed for "deep cleaning" after an Earth child was treated there in secret.
New archive link "catches forgers in seconds", says Lattice. Forgers "now inventing better names".
Invented citizen "Pell-Ruu Nobody" seen dining on floor 21. Lattice: "A typo."
Archive records now link every window in the Tower. "We know who you are," says the Lattice. "Probably."
Duun of Maintenance wins "Most Talkative Employee" for the ninth cycle running.
Files going down to the archive "faster than ever". Up? "That's not a direction files go."
Lattice inspector "accidentally arrested during a test". Window under review.
Windows pass surprise inspections "with distinction". One receptionist named "reliable".
Ruu clan protests wanted bulletins: "Our stalks are not a disguise."
The Lattice confirms it does not send inspectors. Inspectors confirm they are not being sent.
Refugee camp beyond the Moss Deeps "dispersed". Where to? "Elsewhere."
"Skilled invaders" now outnumber clumsy ones, says Lattice. "Our windows are better still."
4th-question licences sell out. "Three questions was always too few," admits Lattice.
Earth signal changes: "It sounds like a lullaby," says a moon-reader, who has since resigned.
Crest parade route announced. Lift maintenance "suspended for the festivities".
Parade night arrests: four humans "cheered too loudly".
Humans seen dancing at the crest parade. "Badly," adds the Lattice.
Plo frill-crowns win the parade for a 10th cycle. Ruu stalk-seers demand a recount.
Cycle 413 ends. Lattice figures: "invaders down, invaders up, invaders stable".
A Tower lift was heard going down during the parade fireworks. "Fireworks," says the Lattice.
SABOTAGE on floor 9: audit records burned. Lattice blames "an Earth spy who got past a window".
Earth spy caught at Tower carrying "devices". Lattice: "Proof they are all dangerous."
Not every human is a refugee, says Lattice. Not every refugee is human, says nobody.
Ammaru clan outraged by wanted bulletin: "Three eyes, zero crimes."
The audit office is now closed "until the audit is audited".
Arrests at the Tower reach a record. The basement is "at capacity", says a leaked memo. There is no memo.
Rumours of "a quiet door" at the Tower spread through the Moss Deeps.
Stamp rule moves to Plo visitors. Ammaru stamp-makers "30% relieved".
Lattice: "There is no basement." Lift engineers: "There is definitely a basement."
Cycle 414 begins with three new rules and a fourth "to be announced".
Human "face-copier" caught minutes after the real citizen passed. "Like looking in a bad mirror."
Orr-Vessi Talm reports "another me" on floor 2. Lattice: "Are you sure it wasn't you?"
The real Orr-Vessi Talm arrested at the Tower. His copy was let in. Lattice: "A mix-up."
Face-copying forgers "the new threat". Citizens urged not to have common faces.
Service shaft workers report "voices". Voices report nothing.
The Clinic reopens. Earth child "returned to where she came from". Where? "Elsewhere."
Woman with a stolen processing file arrested at the Tower. File returned "unread".
Second inspector arrested at the same window. Graav: "No comment."
Missing Records files "probably misfiled". Probably.
Lattice confirms basement "does not exist and is fully staffed".
Kesh glows an odd colour over the Moss Deeps. Moon-readers: "Smoke."
Curfew "a success": fewer appointments, more arrests per appointment.
Families left queuing at the Tower at closing time. "Come back before midnight," says Lattice.
CURFEW: no appointments after midnight. Night-shift workers told to "get sick earlier".
Lattice Clinic offers free gill scans to all Tower staff. "Routine," it insists.
Plo clan elder Pluvia: "The rules change faster than the moon."
Vessi-suited humans "everywhere", says Lattice. Vessi: "We are everywhere. We live here."
The Earth signal falls silent. Moon-readers: "That's worse."
Maintenance logs "temporarily confiscated" across the Tower.
Night Window staff to be "reviewed one by one" before the Grand Audit.
Graav watched Night Window 3 from the gallery all night. "Educational," he says.
Night Window 3 "exemplary" under supervision. Graav "almost smiles".
Stamp rule moves to Vessi visitors. Vessi stamp-makers "90% busy".
Lattice publishes list of "invader behaviours": blinking, laughing, hoping.
Grand Audit scheduled for the end of the cycle. "Every window. Every decision."
Second face-copier caught. "The eyes in the photo," says a receptionist. "Always the eyes."
Real citizen arrested as their own copy. "I have never been less myself," says Dosk-Plo Phae.
Forgers now copying faces "from the archive itself". Archive "looking into it".
Refugees seen boarding a ship at the Moss Deeps. Ship destination: "anywhere but Earth".
The lift log of the Tower has gone missing. Lattice: "There was never a log."
Third inspector arrested at Night Window 3. The window is "a problem", says the Lattice.
Cycle 414 ends. The Lattice thanks every citizen for being 60% content.
Graav seen carrying a lift log to the basement. "There is no basement," he tells reporters.
Audit and Housing closed. Residents of floor 21 "temporarily rehoused" downstairs.
Lockdown night: arrests at the Tower "higher than ever, as planned".
LOCKDOWN: Audit and Records sealed. The Grand Auditor arrives tomorrow.
Stamp rule moves to Ruu visitors. "It's a lottery," says a stamp-maker.
Rumour: the Grand Auditor will "personally test the windows".
GRAND AUDITOR ARRESTED AT NIGHT WINDOW 3. Released after 40 minutes. "A thorough window," he says, through his teeth.
Grand Auditor passes through the Tower "without incident". Windows "adequate".
The Grand Audit begins in two nights. Every receptionist's record will be read aloud.
Families queue for clinic passes before the Grand Audit lockdown.
The Earth signal returns, one word repeated: "Please."
Tower receptionist calls security on own sibling. "Rules are rules," says Lattice, approvingly.
TOMORROW: THE GRAND AUDIT. The Tower locks down at 02:00.
Every lift in the Tower freshly oiled. "Suspiciously quiet," says Graav.
Moon-readers predict Kesh "will be decisive" tomorrow.

messages.text: Three strikes in the Basement act. The hearing found your mistakes honest — this time. Fined 30 shards. I read your answer logs, Ilo. If I ever find a slip you ignored, the next hearing is your last.
Three strikes this act. Disciplinary hearing held in your absence: fined 30 shards. Your slate is clean. It will not be clean twice.
Your sibling Sel was admitted last night with gill fever. Sel is resting at home now. The 50-shard bill is due tonight.
You owe me rent, Receptionist. I am 0% patient. Pay, or the Lattice hears about it.
Welcome to the Lattice Tower, Receptionist Ilo. Report to Night Window 3 at 20:00. You are paid per correct decision; errors are deducted. Glory to the Lattice.
BIG NIGHT!! You're going to be the best window person ever. I'm 90% proud and 10% coughing. Don't worry about the coughing. Will you bring me a story about a weird visitor?

choices.reply: YES. 100% asleep. (Not really.)

choices.text: Work is work, Sel. Rules are rules.
choices.reply: ...okay. 60% okay.

messages.text: A clean first night. Don't let it go to your crest.
Mistakes on your first night. Everyone makes them once. Make them once.
Did you see one?? A real human?? Tuvo at school says they have hair EVERYWHERE and five fingers on each hand. FIVE.
Rent is due every night, Receptionist. The Lattice pays you; you pay me. Simple.
I'm fine. I'm 40% fine. The cough is louder at night, but I can hide it under the pillow.
The new medicine tastes like burnt glow-moss. I'm 70% better! Did anyone laugh at your jokes yet?
You arrested a citizen. Their family filed a complaint with my office. Read the rulebook. Then read it again.
Receptionist. You work for the Lattice, yes? The family in 22-B never shows their gills. Never. I've been watching. Will you report them?

choices.text: I'll pass it on to the Lattice.
choices.reply: Good. Someone has to.

choices.text: Leave them alone. Gills are private.
choices.reply: Hmph. On your crest be it.

messages.text: Don't be mad. I fainted at school. The nurse says I need my medicine every night. Every night, Ilo.
I drew you at your window! You're the one with the big important face. Graav is the grumpy cloud.
Records is closed tomorrow. Make them breathe on the glass. Citizens leave it clear.
You're good at spotting us. Do you know where they take the ones you catch? Look down, receptionist. — W3

choices.reply: (The message is gone. The feeling isn't.)
Someone who sat at Window 3 once. Like you. — W3

messages.text: Some of us walked right past you. Maybe you noticed, maybe you didn't. Either way: thank you. Look down, receptionist. — W3

choices.reply: (The message is gone. The feeling isn't.)
Someone who sat at Window 3 once. Like you. — W3

messages.text: A Lattice man came to school and asked if anyone's family blinks. Everyone laughed. I didn't laugh. Is that bad?
Your first week is done. Tomorrow the clan rule starts: Ammaru need a blue stamp. Know the clans better than they do.
Tomorrow the forgers start faking holograms. A UV lamp shows the fakes. The Lattice store sells them. I'd buy one.
Is it true the humans' planet is dying? Tuvo says they come here because there's nowhere else. Tuvo says a lot of things.
You came home late again. I saved you some spore-meal. It's 50% spore-meal and 50% my drawing of you.
You closed the window with visitors still queuing. They complain to me, not to you. Faster tomorrow.
Tomorrow's bulletin names the Vessi. A wanted list is a hint, not a verdict. I've seen windows arrest a whole clan on a hint.
A note under your door, in careful, square handwriting: "Twice now. My brother was taken at your window before you came. His file is on 14. If you ever see the name SELK, think of me. — M."

choices.reply: (The paper curls. The name stays with you: SELK.)
(You fold it small. Sel's drawings hide it nicely.)

messages.text: Can I ask a weird thing? I peeked when you were asleep. You close your eyes when you sleep. Like, all the way. Tuvo says only humans do that. Tuvo's wrong, right?

choices.text: Everyone does it, Sel. Go to sleep.
choices.reply: Okay. 70% okay.
Your neck. The gill lines are too straight. Like someone drew them. I like them though!

messages.text: You arrested a real citizen because the bulletin said Vessi. The bulletin also says the sky is up. Think.
The Lattice asks landlords about their tenants now. What they eat, when they sleep. I told them you're boring, Receptionist. Stay boring.
Your first cycle is done and your record is good. Good records get noticed upstairs. Some things upstairs are better not noticed. Keep it good anyway.
Your first cycle is done. Your record has… gaps. Humans walk through your window, and you don't call me. I'm writing that down.
New cycle, receptionist. You've seen enough of us now to know we're not monsters. Some of us are running from a dying world. Some of us are not. Can we talk? — W3

choices.text: Report the message to the Lattice.
choices.reply: (A Lattice clerk thanks you. Your message is "filed".)
Good. Watch for a courier with a blue thread on their cuff. — W3

messages.text: New cycle! I'm 80% better and 100% bored. Can you bring home a story about a nice human? Is there such a thing?
Tuvo's family moved away. Overnight. The teacher said "reassigned". Tuvo's mum blinked a lot, I think. Was that why?
You reported a contact from "Window 3". Good. Most windows don't. If they write again, tell me first.
The gill-scope ads are everywhere. Should we get one for home? Just to check… you know. Nobody. Just to check.
A courier came through your window tonight. Blue thread on the cuff. Whatever you did, we saw it. — W3
I'm 70% better! The medicine tastes like burnt moss AND old lanterns now. Progress.
Rent goes up next cycle. Lattice says landlords must "verify tenants' gills". I'm not doing that. Rent still goes up.
There's a wire under your desk that isn't on any plan. Connect it and you'll have a button. Press it instead of calling security, and we take them somewhere safe. Nobody upstairs sees a thing. — W3

choices.reply: Then we're in this together. Press it only when you're sure. — W3
Then do it well. We'll still be here. — W3

messages.text: Rumours say someone is turning the night windows. If anyone offers you anything, you tell me.
Can we go to Lantern Night tomorrow? Oh. You work. Can I go with Vaun's kids? They're 40% nice.
I found a photo in the old drawer. A woman with ROUND eyes holding a baby, in a blanket with stars on it. Is that from your work?

choices.text: Put it back, Sel. It's nothing.
choices.reply: Okay. It's back. (It's not nothing. She looks like you.)
On the back it says "Tower, C393. Keep her safe." Who's "her"? Who's the baby, Ilo?

messages.text: I found my brother's file on 14. And another one, filed right behind it. A baby left at this Tower, cycle 393. Adopted by an Ammaru family. The baby's name was ILO. — M.

choices.reply: (You burn it. You remember every word.)
"Mother: unknown. Species: see attached." The attachment was missing. — M.

messages.text: You have the archive now. Use it. A name with no record is a person who doesn't exist. People who don't exist don't complain.
Cough's back. Don't buy food for me tomorrow, buy medicine. I can eat spore-meal crumbs. I'm small.
I went to Lantern Night! Everyone's lanterns were the same colour except one kid's. The guards took his family. Why do they care about lanterns?
You arrested my inspector. He blinked, yes. He had a pass, yes. Read. The. Pass. It's in your file now.
My inspector says you read his pass. Officially, I don't have inspectors. Unofficially: good.
Vaun's kids say the blinking people go to the basement and become lanterns. That's not true, right? Right?
You should know something about Window 3, receptionist. The one before you was human. So was the one before her. — W3

choices.reply: Because you should ask who put you there, and why they never check your eyes. — W3

messages.text: You got a 4th question licence? Ask Graav what's in the basement. Ask him four times.
PARADE!!! The Plo won AGAIN. I cheered for the Ruu. Somebody has to.
Too many humans walk through your window, Ilo. Either you're careless or you're kind. The Lattice doesn't have a word for kind.
End of cycle. Your record holds. Next cycle the rules tighten, and so will I.
The man you let in burned the audit office. A spy, not a refugee. Now do you see why we check?
Not all of us are running from something. The one who burned floor 9 wasn't ours. We're sorry. — W3
New cycle! You look tired. Like 30% tired. I'm making you a lantern. It'll be whatever colour you want.
Act three of your career, receptionist. From now on, a hearing isn't a fine. It's the end of you. Three strikes. Count them.
Do you ever wonder if we're the strange ones? Like, from the outside? Tuvo used to say that. Before.
We know what's downstairs now. Processing. The people you report go down in the service lift, and they don't come back up. — W3

choices.reply: Then get it. Someone in the Tower keeps a log of every trip down. — W3
Nobody does. That's how it works. — W3

messages.text: There were two of the same man at the clinic today! Same face! One of them blinked. I didn't tell anyone. Was that right?
As promised. A copy of my brother's processing record: the date he was taken down, the room, the order signed by the Lattice. — M.

choices.reply: (You tape it under Sel's drawer. Proof. Real proof.)
(The paper curls. His name goes with it.)

messages.text: Window 3 got me out with the file. Here's a copy for you: proof of what's downstairs. — M.

choices.reply: (Proof. Under Sel's drawer.)

messages.text: Second inspector, second arrest. Still gills, valid pass. You don't read, Ilo. You react.
I'm drawing everyone at the Tower. Duun has the best face. Graav has the worst face. You have a nice face. A weird nice face.
Routine gill scan for Tower staff, Receptionist Ilo: "Gill lines unusually regular. Scar tissue at the neck consistent with…" The rest of the report is marked RESTRICTED.

choices.reply: (Routine. Everything is routine.)

choices.text: Ask the nurse what it means.
choices.reply: The nurse looks at your eyes for a long time. "Surgical," she says quietly. "Very old. Very good work."

messages.text: Curfew means the clinic shuts at midnight. I'll be fine. 50% fine.
Curfew. Lattice says lights out at midnight. Your lamp was on till 03:00. I didn't see it. This time.
The Earth song stopped. I liked it. Is it bad that I liked it?
Tomorrow I watch your window from the gallery. All night. Give me a reason, Ilo. I'm hoping you won't.
Duun from Maintenance kept a copy of the lift log. Every trip down, every name. He'll hand it to someone he trusts. Is that you? — W3

choices.reply: Duun slips you the log in a lantern box. "80% scared," he whispers. "20% proud."
Then we wait. Waiting is also a choice. — W3

messages.text: Graav came to Block 22 today and asked the landlord about us. He was 0% friendly. Are we in trouble?
Copied faces. Copied names. Copied papers. The only thing they can't copy is how a citizen behaves. Watch behaviour.
No medicine again. It's okay. I know it's expensive. I know you're trying.
Three inspectors. Three arrests. At the Grand Audit, that number will be read aloud.
Next cycle I'm going to apply for the Tower junior programme. I want to be a window person. Like you!
The Grand Auditor arrives tomorrow and will test the windows in person. Do your job. Just your job. Nothing extra.
The Grand Audit is our one chance. Every lift in the Tower opens for the inspection. If the city sees the basement, it can't pretend anymore. Get ready. — W3
You arrested the Grand Auditor. He was released. You will not be, if it happens again.
I have a clinic appointment tomorrow night. At YOUR window! Is that allowed? I'm bringing you dinner. Don't tell Graav.
Tomorrow at 02:00, open the service lift for us. With proof, the city sees the basement. Without it… we just walk into a trap. Your choice, Ilo. — W3

choices.reply: Then tomorrow, everything changes. — W3
Then thank you for everyone you already let through. — W3

messages.text: Do tomorrow right and floor 9 is yours. An office. A real salary. Sel's medicine, every night, for life. Think about it.

choices.reply: Good. Don't make me regret it.
(He waits. You don't answer.)

messages.text: Tomorrow's the big night! Whatever happens at the Tower, I'm 100% proud of you. Even if you blink. I know you blink. It's okay.
Your sibling Sel was released from Tower security at 03:00 and is resting at home. Sel has not said a word since. Sel left your dinner on the table.
GRAND AUDIT NOTICE. All Night Window staff report at 20:00. Every decision tonight will be reviewed. At 02:00 the Tower locks down. Glory to the Lattice.

upgrades.name: UV lamp
upgrades.text: Shows genuine holograms: real ones glow with rings, printed fakes stay flat.

upgrades.name: Gill-scope
upgrades.text: Shows the neck up close: real gills pulse, a suit's gills sit still.

upgrades.name: 4th question licence
upgrades.text: One more question for every visitor.

steps.text: Welcome to Night Window 3! Every visitor says they're a citizen of Vel'Tara. Some are HUMANS hiding in stolen bio-suits. Your job: spot them.
This is their Civic Lattice ID. First check: does the PHOTO match the face at the window? Same clan, same face, slit pupils.
This is their appointment slip. The NAME must match the ID exactly, and the FLOOR must be in the ID's floor access.
Up here: tonight's date, the clock and your score. An ID that EXPIRES before tonight's date is no good.
You can ask each visitor 3 questions. Pick one now. Try “How are you feeling tonight?”
Every answer goes in this log. Citizens state a mood, like “I am 60% content.”
Not sure what's normal? The RULEBOOK lists how citizens look and behave, and every desk rule.
Matching papers, a matching face, a citizen's answer. This is a citizen: press LET IN.
Look closely at this visitor's eyes: ROUND pupils! Every citizen has vertical slit pupils.
Ask how they're feeling, and read the answer.
“Fine” instead of a mood: another human slip. Humans also blink, sweat, and show five fingers.
This is a human in a suit. HOLD Call Security until the bar fills.
This one looks like a real citizen. But compare the ID's EXPIRES date with tonight's date at the top.
The ID has expired. A real citizen who breaks a rule is TURNED AWAY, never arrested.
That's the job. Humans: CALL SECURITY. Rule-breakers: TURN AWAY. Everyone else: LET IN. The rest of tonight is up to you!
